title: Tastiness Index: Max Minus Min
statement:
A cafeteria rates each of its `n` dishes with an integer tastiness score. The **Tastiness Index** of the menu is the difference between the highest score and the lowest score among all dishes: `max - min`.

Given the scores, compute the Tastiness Index. Scores may be negative or repeated. If the menu has a single dish, or all scores are equal, the index is `0`.
inputFormat:
The first line contains an integer `n`.
The second line contains `n` space-separated integers, the scores.
outputFormat: Print a single integer: the Tastiness Index.

examples.explanation: The highest score is 9 and the lowest is 1, so the index is 9 - 1 = 8.
The highest score is -2 and the lowest is -9, so the index is -2 - (-9) = 7.
With one dish the maximum and minimum are the same value.

hints: You do not need to sort anything: you only need two numbers from the array.
Scan once, keeping the largest and smallest value seen so far.
The difference can reach 2 * 10^9, so make sure your integer type is wide enough (64-bit in C++/Java).
